entities.summary: Šipan is an island located in southern Croatia and part of the city of Dubrovnik, the capital of the Dubrovnik-Neretva County. It is located 17 km (11 mi) northwest of Dubrovnik, and is separated from the mainland coast by the Koločep Channel, which has an area of 16.22 km2 (6.3 sq mi). The island is 9.1 km (5.7 mi) in length, and up to 2.6 km (1.6 mi) in width. It is a part of the Elaphiti Islands, and is the largest island in the archipelago. The name of the archipelago comes from the Ancient Greek word for deer, which, according to Pliny the Elder, used to inhabit the Elaphiti Islands in large numbers.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: Šipan's historical importance lies in its role as part of the Elaphiti Islands, a significant regional archipelago that was once home to large numbers of deer, according to Pliny the Elder. The islands' unique geography and ecosystem have made them an important location for scientific study and conservation efforts.
